Applicants for visas and extensions of stay for study using sponsor acceptances, by education sector, 2010 to year ending December 2024
Total visas - Tertiary, Further education or other colleges
Total extensions - Tertiary, Further education or other colleges
Total unknown - Tertiary, Further education or other colleges
1. A higher education institution (HEI) is a 'recognised body' (meaning that it has its own UK degree-awarding powers), or a body in receipt of public funding as a HEI. Institutions (including
further education colleges) which receive some public funding to deliver higher education courses do not fall within this definition of an HEI.

2. Russell Group describe themselves as representing 24 leading UK universities (http://russellgroup.ac.uk/). A list of these universities can be found in the User Guide to Home Office Immigration System Statistics.

3. Tertiary, Further education or other colleges includes the remainder of sponsors who described themselves as ‘University and tertiary’, plus those who described themselves as ‘Private Institution of Further or Higher Education’
or whose self-description included ‘Further education’ or ‘Higher Education’. This category includes a small number of foreign based universities but these account for very small numbers of CAS used.
4. Other - This category contains all other sponsors, accounting for very small numbers.
5. Changes to the immigration rules redefined the description of the immigration category in December 2020 from "Tier 4 (Sponsored study)" to "Sponsored study (previously Tier 4)".
6. Some cases from Q4 2019 onwards are unable to be separately identified as either a visa or extension case (see notes) and so have been categorised as ‘unknown’.
